title: Unbounded Operators, Physicality, and Modality in Quantum Theories
abstract: In this paper, I address the problem regarding the physicality of Hilbert space in quantum mechanics, a topic brought into focus by Carcassi et al.'s paper "The unphysicality of Hilbert spaces" recently. I argue for the physicality of the Hilbert space in quantum mechanics, and demonstrate that there are inevitable ambiguity and arbitrariness if we want to identify the set of physical states with a proper subset of it. Moreover, I distinguish the ontological and modal reading of physicality from the pragmatic and operational reading of physicality, and then develop what I call the hierarchical view of physicality. According to this view, physicality is not a monolithic concept, but a layered one that admits degrees. I show the connection between the concept of physicality and modal metaphysics, and finally explain how it can be used to address the interpretational problem of quantum field theory brought by the existence of inequivalent representations.
summary: This paper tackles deep foundational questions regarding what constitutes a 'physical' state in quantum theory, especially when operators are unbounded. The author develops a hierarchical view of physicality, arguing that physical reality is not monolithic but layered. This framework is used to critique existing arguments and to provide a potential resolution for interpretational problems in Quantum Field Theory.
main_problem: The paper tackles the foundational issue of the physicality of the Hilbert space in quantum mechanics, particularly when dealing with unbounded operators and defining the set of physical states.
main_result: The author proposes a hierarchical view of physicality, arguing that physicality is layered and admits degrees, which helps reconcile foundational issues in quantum field theory.
method: The methodology involves distinguishing between ontological/modal and pragmatic/operational readings of physicality, and applying modal metaphysics to quantum structures.
model_or_system: The discussion centers on standard quantum mechanics axioms, the position and Hamiltonian operators, and extends to the algebraic structures of Quantum Field Theory (QFT) involving the Weyl algebra.
key_observables: Position operator expectation values ($\langle x angle_\psi$), probability distributions of measurement results, and the structure of physical states defined by normal states in QFT.
important_parameters: The distinction between potential and actual infinities, and the nature of singularities versus the existence of infinite expectation values.
main_assumptions: The paper assumes that the difficulties raised by restricting the state space (e.g., by Heathcote or Carcassi et al.) are artifacts of an overly rigid interpretation of physical axioms.
figures_summary: The figures illustrate the hierarchy of logical, metaphysical, and physical possible worlds, suggesting multiple, nested structures of physical possibility.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first addressing the Hilbert space physicality problem with unbounded operators, then applying this framework to critique arguments regarding infinite expectation values in position measurements, and finally extending the hierarchical view to resolve interpretational issues in QFT.
why_interesting: While highly abstract, the development of a 'hierarchical view of physicality' provides a novel meta-framework for interpreting foundational inconsistencies arising in advanced quantum theories, which is relevant to understanding the limits of current quantum descriptions.
